Inside the generator, paired-path alignment creates an interface block through which post-training routes noise, and the image semantics carried through it predict sample quality across 16 models. The resulting recipe, \method, accelerates \emph{both} training stages on ImageNet $256\!\times\!256$: it matches the 160-epoch baseline with $2\times$ fewer priming epochs, surpasses its final quality with $4\times$ fewer post-training updates, and lowers FID to 1.30 (B) and 1.155 (L) at the standard budget. A joint single-stage variant trains native one-step generators and reaches FID 1.22 with 115M parameters.
item.dc:creator: Mingxiao Li, Xuantuo Huang, Encheng Su, Aoran Wang, Han Zhang, Jinouwen Zhang, Shixiang Tang

item.title: GUI-Q: Task-Sensitive Granularity and Relation-Preserving Quantization for GUI Agents
item.description: arXiv:2611.30170v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Graphical user interface (GUI) agents enable automated interactions with mobile, web, and desktop interfaces. However, their large memory footprint and repeated model calls hinder deployment on resource-constrained devices, motivating post-training quantization (PTQ) without full retraining. Quantization can degrade GUI response accuracy and distort the instruction-vision affinities and local spatial relations needed for GUI target selection. Small coordinate errors can cause missed clicks, while early action errors can alter subsequent interface states and disrupt task execution. Local reconstruction error alone does not directly assess whether these responses and relations are preserved. We propose GUI-Q, a PTQ framework that targets response and relation preservation with 4-bit weights and 16-bit activations (W4A16). Task-Sensitive Granularity Allocation (TSGA) allocates finer groups under a scale-byte budget by combining response sensitivity with the measured reduction in activation-weighted distortion. Relation-Preserving Symmetry Selection (RPSS) then selects symmetric or asymmetric grids to preserve instruction-vision affinities and local spatial relations in GUIs. Across three GUI-capable models, GUI-Q improves mean grounding TargetHit by 8.04 to 12.55 points over the strongest evaluated 4-bit configurations, while reducing static peak graphics processing unit (GPU) memory by 49.9% to 56.2% relative to bfloat16 (BF16). Fixed-output replay with packed 4-bit execution provides 1.7 to 2.8 times model-call speedups. The code will be released.
item.dc:creator: Tianqi Li, Yang Wang, Xin He, Le Zhang, Yun Liu

item.title: OmniSenMo: A Unified Multisensory Language Model for Generalizable Human Motion Estimation, Understanding, and Prediction
item.description: arXiv:2611.30176v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) estimate, understand, and predict human motion, but mainly from RGB cameras. Depth, LiDAR, mmWave, and WiFi complement RGB under poor lighting, through occlusions, and in privacy-sensitive applications, but existing multisensory models cover only some of these sensing tasks. Covering all of them from any sensor subset is challenging, since the tokens of heterogeneous sensors are semantically inconsistent and spatially misaligned, paired multisensory data are scarce, and the tasks need different temporal granularities. We present OmniSenMo, a multisensory language model that takes the human skeleton as a common reference for all sensors. Its skeleton-grounded motion representation turns each sensor into joint tokens, one per body joint, so that any sensor subset is fused joint by joint and expressed in the motion vocabulary that the language model learned from motion capture and text. We pretrain it on all five sensors generated by our multisensory simulator, and Multi-Granularity Observation gives each task the frames it needs. On a cross-action split of MM-Fi, the same model with all five sensors outperforms the models compared on each task, including LEO-Fuse in pose estimation (84.1 vs. 89.0 mm MPJPE) and HoloLLM in unseen-action recognition (69.2% vs. 42.8%). Even without RGB, it outperforms both methods that use RGB, and in a cross-dataset validation on XRF55, it recognizes unseen actions far better than HoloLLM.
item.dc:creator: Cheng Guo, Qiming Cao, Pu Perry Wang, Pu Wang, Hongfei Xue

item.title: Quantization for Action, Execution for Deployment: Joint Precision and Execution Selection for World Action Models
item.description: arXiv:2611.30195v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: World action models guide robots by predicting the effects of actions or generating commands from observations. A model may compare hundreds of candidate futures before acting, repeatedly reading weights that must fit in device memory. Post-training quantization reduces the number of bits used to store pretrained weights, but a smaller model is not necessarily a deployable one: temporary tensors can exceed graphics processing unit (GPU) memory limits, while even small prediction errors can change the selected action. This creates two coupled challenges: identifying bit assignments that preserve task performance and determining which of them meet real execution constraints, without exhausting costly task trials. We present PTQ4WAM, a framework for choosing layer-wise bit assignments and execution routes under memory, latency and task-evaluation budgets. Calibration measurements guide candidate proposals, optionally with a language model agent. We profile full-model routes on the GPU before spending task trials on feasible assignments. Fusing group rescaling and reading visual history in place can make an otherwise infeasible assignment deployable. Across 15 workloads from four model families, the median task score is 99.2% of the corresponding 32-bit floating-point (FP32) score. On fixed GPU replays, the median speedup over FP32 is 2.36 times and the median reduction in peak allocated memory is 71.5%. The code will be released soon.
item.dc:creator: Tianqi Li, Xin He, Xue Geng, Le Zhang, Ming-Ming Cheng, Yun Liu

item.title: PinGround: Pinning Queries to Points for Parallel Grounding in Vision-Language Models
item.description: arXiv:2611.30304v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can localize through their text interface, grounding open-vocabulary objects, complex referring expressions, text lines and layout regions with strong semantic understanding. They write the boxes one after another as a single sequence, although the instances of a query, unlike the words of a sentence, form an unordered set with no sequential dependence. The number of decoding steps therefore grows with the number of instances, which makes dense scenes the most expensive. Decoding the instances in parallel avoids this growth, but streams that cannot see each other duplicate some instances and miss others. We propose PinGround, which writes a single point into each query as a spatial anchor and asks for the matching instance nearest to that point within a local radius, or None. Given the image, the anchored queries are independent, so they are decoded in parallel as leaves of a prefix tree that shares the image and the query, and the model is trained on the same tree. Coarse-to-fine anchors refine only the regions where instances are found, duplicate suppression keeps one box per instance, and set-level reinforcement learning optimizes the set F1. Only the prompt and the attention mask change, not the architecture. On three different VLMs and 12 benchmarks covering detection, OCR, layout and referring, PinGround is at most 5.5 F1 below sequential decoding trained on the same data, while its speedup grows with instance density and reaches 21.9$\times$ on dense scenes.
item.dc:creator: Shuxuan Li, Jialiang Kang, Yanghao Zhou, Ziye Zhu, Zhilin Zhao, Xiao Yang

item.title: CineAct: Interaction-State Agents for Playable, Branching Film Generation
item.description: arXiv:2611.30613v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Open video generators such as MiniMax-H3 produce short clips of only several to a dozen seconds per run. To synthesize longer sequences, existing methods either rely on agentic systems following preset scripts, or roll out autoregressively from the previous clip's last frame, losing off-screen states and accumulating hallucinations across turns. Consequently, users still cannot take an explicit goal, choose how to accomplish it, and see that choice persist across subsequent clips. We study goal-grounded interactive video generation, where one goal admits multiple valid approaches, the user's chosen approach must be executed on screen, and its consequences must persist across clips. To this end, we propose CineAct, a state-first agentic framework in which language-model agents handle reasoning while frozen image and video generators serve purely as renderers. Before interaction, the Architect initializes the world as a spatial layout with cameras, an asset library, and a scene graph; at each turn, the system deduces the planned state change, generates a target end frame with an image generator and rigorously verifies it, and synthesizes intermediate motion with an FL2V model. We further introduce a multi-space benchmark covering two suites: long-horizon step execution and open-intent branching admissibility. Experiments show that explicit world-state modeling boosts multi-step rollout consistency over the pixel-only baseline (+11.4 automated, +23.1 human points) and raises paired branching success toward a shared goal by +30.8 points.
item.dc:creator: Junyan Lin, Jianqi Ma, Shujie Duan, Hanxin Zhu, Zhihao Hu, Jinming Liu, Shuai Li, Jun Zhang, Xin Jin, Chang Wen Chen, Weidong Zhang

item.title: G0.7: Scaling Up a Fast World Action Model with Long Context
item.description: arXiv:2611.31822v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: World action models (WAMs) adapt pretrained video generators for robot control by jointly predicting future camera frames and actions, transferring physical priors learned from video into manipulation policies. However, generating future frames before every action makes test-time inference too slow for closed-loop control, while most existing policies remain restricted to short observation histories. Building on Fast-WAM, which showed that video prediction shapes policy representations during training so that future frame synthesis can be skipped at deployment, we present G0.7, a generalist world action model scaled along two axes: extending the context window from a single observation to up to five minutes of history, and scaling pretraining to a large-scale corpus of robot teleoperation and human egocentric (ego) video. Across public simulation suites and real-robot deployments, direct action decoding (Fast mode) matches imagine-then-act (IDM) inference from the same checkpoint while running in 60 ms per 16-step action chunk on a single RTX 5090 (7.6x faster than IDM) and supporting pause-free real-time chunking. Performance scales consistently with pretraining data, with human ego video driving the largest gains in out-of-distribution generalization: G0.7 achieves a 70.8 mean score across five simulation benchmark suites, 48% and 54% zero-shot pick-and-place success on Galaxea R1 Pro and R1 Lite, 96.7% in-distribution and 93.3% out-of-distribution success on video-conditioned in-context learning tasks, and 86.9% mean task progress across seven real-world post-training tasks including multi-minute box folding, drink preparation, and product bagging. Project page: https://www.galaxea-ai.com/model-g07.html
item.dc:creator: Tianyuan Yuan, Baijun Ye, Shicheng Cao, Xing Nie, Xiaopeng Yu, Ke Dong, Zijie Zhao, Shenling Qiu, Yizhao Xu, Feiyang Xue, Haonan Liu, Haoyu Zhang, Haobo Jia, Zheng Liu, Bowen Zhang, Haodong Yang, Anqi Yang, Jiahui Niu, Yue Sun, Tailai Cheng, Jianpeng Yu, Yang Wen, Longhao Wei, Zibin Dong, Shiduo Zhang, Yicheng Liu, Hang Zhao

item.title: EditText: Structure-Aware Generation and Selective Visual Transport for Fine-Grained Text Editing
item.description: arXiv:2611.32134v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Fine-grained text editing aims to accurately replace text in a specified region while preserving the source text's font, color, and texture, as well as visual consistency in unedited regions. We present EditText, a unified framework for fine-grained text editing that combines target character generation with visual transport from the source image. The model uses dual-condition Fill inputs: a masked image and a source text style reference, both sharing a spatial reference with the target image. The masked image hides the original text and retains unedited content as a source canvas; the style reference supplies appearance cues that guide new character generation together with the target text. We introduce an Attention Transport framework in which Source Weight describes the attention allocated to a condition and the Spatial Aggregation Kernel describes its internal spatial attention distribution. Accurate transfer of source details depends on attention strength, the retention of details in condition features, and spatially accurate aggregation. For selected non-edit queries, we therefore preserve the total attention weight assigned to the masked image while redistributing its attention toward spatially corresponding neighborhoods, enabling selective visual transport. Multi-stage training, combined with a Glyph-aware Structural Loss on local target character structure, teaches the model to generate accurate text, preserve source text appearance, and retain unedited details. We also introduce TBench, a fine-grained text editing benchmark covering Alphabetic, Logographic, and Arabic numerals, to evaluate character updates, appearance preservation, and the preservation of unedited details. On TBench, EditText achieves state-of-the-art non-edit-region SSIM (0.9769) and full-image LPIPS (0.0460).
item.dc:creator: Zhaobin Chu, Guandong Li, Xin Lv, Zhiwei Zeng

item.title: MediaStormBench-CameraLog: Can Multimodal Models Identify a Camera's Log Curve?
item.description: arXiv:2611.32172v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: MediaStormBench is a multimodal benchmark for real-world film and television production, with each subset drawn from MediaStorm's day-to-day work. We release its first subset, MediaStormBench-CameraLog (CameraLogBench), on a common foundational task in footage ingest and initial color grading: identifying the Log curve of a clip without metadata. Cameras record Log footage by compressing a wide range of scene light into code values with a vendor-defined logarithmic curve, and color can be restored correctly only once that curve is known. The curve, however, is recorded only in file metadata, easily lost in transcoding and team hand-offs. A colorist then has to try candidate curves one by one against a waveform scope, and a wrong choice shifts the tones and colors of the whole clip. Recovering the curve from the image alone is challenging, because vendor curves cluster tightly in code value and are coupled with unknown exposure. CameraLogBench is built on professionally shot footage and tests whether multimodal models can identify the curve, with a probe that removes the correct option to expose guessing from priors. Because every candidate curve is strictly defined by a published vendor formula, we derive four controls from one implementation of these formulas: graded negatives, synthetic frames of identical scenes, in-context specification digests, and a training-free formula baseline, which together decouple semantic priors from photometric measurement. Across 11 models, real-footage accuracy barely exceeds always guessing the most frequent curve; when the correct option is removed, models almost never abstain, revealing heavy reliance on scene and brand priors. Supplying the vendor specification sharply improves recognition on calibrated charts but hardly helps on natural images without a photometric reference, exposing a gap between reading a specification and measuring pixels.
item.dc:creator: Ming Ma, Wenhao Hu, Qichao Wang, Yuhao Wang, Junpeng Zhao, Qiyi Wang, Fangrui Zhang, Zhiqian Lai, Shanxin Guan, Haoyi Pei, Hongan Chen, Rui Gong

item.title: What to Change, What to Keep: Experience-Evolving Agents for Video Recasting
item.description: arXiv:2611.32196v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Video recasting aims to transform the entities and environments of existing videos into new visual worlds while preserving their essential actions and interactions. However, achieving coherent transformations remains challenging, as coordinated edits can disrupt the original event structure. In this paper, we introduce RecastAgent, an experience-guided agentic framework for source-conditioned video recasting that operates under frozen model weights. Our framework employs an Experience-Guided Planner to choose edit prompts and input video states under qualitative visual critique, allowing the agent to build upon partial progress or backtrack to preserve source structure. Across tasks, an Experience Accumulation module distills completed trajectories into conditional, evidence-linked principles that record both an editing strategy and its scope of validity. We additionally construct a benchmark of 67 source videos with 134 paired-specification tasks across six creative categories for evaluation. Experiments demonstrate that RecastAgent outperforms single-pass and agentic rewriting baselines across Bernini and Ditto. Furthermore, accumulated experience improves performance on held-out test videos and transfers zero-shot to external benchmarks like FiVE-Bench and VE-Bench.
item.dc:creator: Shiying Zhang, Yuxia Zhu, Huaze Xue, Shengqi Dang, Yizhen Wu, Yijie Li

item.title: MaskedVGGT: Masked Multi-View Transformers Are Scalable 3D Learners
item.description: arXiv:2611.32297v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multi-view feed-forward models show strong scalability, but their reliance on costly geometric annotations limits data scaling. Existing 3D self-supervised approaches reduce this reliance through cross-view completion (e.g., CroCo, MuM, Muskie) or novel-view synthesis (e.g., RayZer, E-RayZer), typically learning image representations and cross-view interactions jointly. We argue that learning single image representations from scratch is unnecessary for 3D pretraining methods, as doing so fails to benefit from the continuing advances in 2D foundation models (e.g., DINO, CLIP, frontier VLMs). We introduce MaskedVGGT, which freezes a strong pretrained 2D encoder and pretrains only an added, randomly initialized multi-view transformer, focusing on learning interactions across views. MaskedVGGT pretrains the multi-view transformer through masked self-distillation without annotations: a student predicts targets at masked locations based on complete anchor views and heavily masked remaining views, while an exponential-moving-average teacher provides prediction targets based on unmasked inputs. In experiments across model sizes up to 1B parameters, MaskedVGGT pretraining followed by fine-tuning outperforms single-stage supervised VGGT-$\Omega$ training with the same training data, model architecture, and total number of optimization updates. MaskedVGGT also outperforms E-RayZer, CroCo, MuM, and Muskie, providing evidence for the effectiveness of building multi-view pretraining on strong 2D representations. Finally, extending pretraining with additional unlabeled videos further improves generalization, and the learned representations transfer to diverse downstream tasks. These results demonstrate an effective division of learning: reuse strong image representations from 2D pretraining and learn cross-view interactions from unlabeled multi-view data without relying on geometric annotations.
item.dc:creator: Zichen Zou, Xiaosong Jia, Wen-Ming Chen, Zuxuan Wu, Yu-Gang Jiang

item.title: SynAVID: A Synthetic Audio-Visual Immersive Dataset of Dynamic Scenes
item.description: arXiv:2611.32311v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Immersive scene modeling requires synchronized visual and auditory observations under changing viewpoints and scene conditions. Obtaining such observations and references for controlled scene changes remains challenging. We introduce SynAVID, a synthetic audio-visual immersive dataset comprising eight indoor and outdoor scenes. Each minute-scale episode combines fixed camera arrays and moving trajectories with synchronized, viewpoint-dependent binaural audio. Shared scene dynamics, sound-source events, and observer poses drive visual rendering and geometry-aware acoustic synthesis. We evaluate existing methods for visual reconstruction, binaural audio reconstruction, and audiovisual editing. Mixed-observation configurations generally improve visual reconstruction on fixed and moving test views, while transiently occupied and sparsely observed regions remain challenging. Methods rank differently on spectral, interaural, and perceptual audio metrics. Geometric and instance annotations expose uneven observation support and local Gaussian representations beyond aggregate scores. Paired references assess target edits and surrounding content, while controlled geometry changes produce listener-dependent acoustic responses. The project page is available at https://avery-xu.github.io/synavid-project/.
item.dc:creator: Jun Xu, Sujing Li, Chunhao Bi, Zhengxue Cheng, Ronghua Wu, Qunshan Gu, Li Song

item.title: ASTERISM: Do Multimodal LLMs Actually Look at All the Images?
item.description: arXiv:2611.32316v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multi-image benchmarks aim to test whether a multimodal large language model (MLLM) combines evidence across images, but many of their items can be answered from a single image. Across about 33k items from 19 public benchmarks, our audit and a two-stage single-image filter find that one image or the question alone settles 24.2% of them. On these items, MLLMs recover from one image a median 78% of the accuracy that all images add over the text alone, so these items reward answering from one image, which we call the single-image shortcut. MLLMs take this shortcut even on items where one image is not enough. On such items, most of their wrong answers repeat an answer they give from one image, at a rate well above chance. We build ASTERISM, to our knowledge the largest audited multi-image benchmark, from these 19 benchmarks by keeping their items that need more than one image. Its 18.7k items, 2.0k of them corrected or rewritten, share one format, one scorer and seven task categories. We also release ASTERISM-Train with 49k training items and ASTERISM-Lite, a hard subset whose items we manually verify one by one. On ASTERISM-Lite, the strongest proprietary MLLM scores 68%. Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR), now common in MLLM post-training, rewards the shortcut as well, because a correct answer read off one image earns as much reward as one that combines images. In line with this, existing RLVR objectives add little to the ASTERISM score. To stop rewarding the shortcut in training as ASTERISM does in evaluation, we propose cross-image credit assignment (CICA), an extension of RLVR that moves the credit toward the tokens that need more than one image. On three open-source MLLMs, CICA raises the ASTERISM score by 2.6 to 6.0 points, more than twice the gain of each general and vision-specific RL objective trained on the same data.
item.dc:creator: Chanseul Cho, Dongwoo Kim, Noori Bae, Seungjae Moon, Seongsu Lee, Youngmin Ro

item.title: GOLD-SLAM: Gaussian-splatting Omnidirectional LiDAR-Depth SLAM
item.description: arXiv:2611.32335v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Panoramic cameras capture nearly the entire spherical field of view in a single frame. However, the mismatch between this panoramic coverage and the field of view of LiDAR poses a substantial challenge for panoramic Gaussian splatting SLAM that relies on LiDAR depth priors. We introduce GOLD-SLAM, a Gaussian-splatting Omnidirectional LiDAR-Depth SLAM system that combines high-quality rendering with accurate geometric reconstruction. It performs tracking and mapping in the spherical domain and uses tracked visual features in regions without LiDAR coverage to improve pose estimation. To address insufficient coverage of newly observed surfaces and floating artifacts during incremental mapping, we introduce Depth-Aware Map Extension and Pruning (DAEP). To enable broader evaluation, we collect a new dataset, WHOLE, using a UAV platform across Weak-geometry, High-dynamic, Omnidirectional, Low-light, and Easy scenarios. Extensive experiments on public benchmarks and WHOLE demonstrate competitive rendering quality and improved geometric accuracy relative to perspective systems. Compared with existing panoramic baselines, GOLD-SLAM improves mean PSNR by 5.56-9.10 dB and reduces mean Depth-L1 by 71.9-83.9%. To assess deployment feasibility on resource-constrained platforms such as UAVs, we evaluate an embedded configuration of GOLD-SLAM on a Jetson Orin NX (16 GB), demonstrating online operation at the cost of reconstruction quality.
item.dc:creator: Weicong Zhang, Yuan Huang, Yu Zheng, Lin Chenxiao, Yingying Li, Lilong Fan, Liangdong Zhuang, Yufan Chen, Ruiping Liu, Junwei Zheng, Jiaming Zhang

item.title: MinPair: Measured Minimal Pairs for Fine-Grained Control in Text-to-Motion Generation
item.description: arXiv:2611.32549v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Text-to-motion generation has made great progress in capturing what action to perform, yet it remains limited in controlling how that action is executed. For example, when only the height word of a kick request changes, none of the tested state-of-the-art methods reaches all three of knee, waist and head height. The other words of a caption usually imply an attribute such as height, so neither the training loss nor the standard metrics require a model to use the word that states it. A model has to use this word only when it alone separates two otherwise identical captions. We introduce MinPair, which creates such caption pairs from real motion clips. It starts from rule-based motion descriptors that measure the 3D body motion of each clip. From these descriptors a language model writes MinPair captions, timed body-part captions that say how each body part moves. The same descriptors show in which attributes two clips of the same action differ. A measured minimal pair joins the true caption of one clip with an altered copy in which only one attribute takes the value measured in the other clip. A contrastive pair loss then requires a diffusion denoiser to reconstruct the clip more accurately from its true caption than from the altered copy. Training needs no synthetic motion and inference stays unchanged. Control is tested on 22 target tasks and on caption edits that each change one attribute. MinPair captions alone help motions reach their targets and improve the standard metrics M2M, R@3 and FID, yet a model trained on them still ignores most single-word edits. The pair loss raises the share of followed template edits from 11% to 60%, while the standard metrics do not improve further. With body-part captions, MinPair reaches more targets than state-of-the-art methods that were trained on up to 99 times more motion data.
item.dc:creator: Lennart Schiweck, Crist\'obal Curio

item.title: EEG-World: Context-Conditioned Dynamics of the Watching Brain
item.description: arXiv:2611.32825v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Brain encoding models predict neural responses from audiovisual input, but typically overlook how ongoing brain activity shapes an individual's response. We introduce EEG-World, a recurrent world model that forecasts 10 seconds of EEG band-power dynamics from 6 seconds of preceding EEG and the subsequent audiovisual stimulus. Pretrained on continuous EEG, EEG-World learns shared neural dynamics and adapts to unseen individuals through lightweight subject-specific readouts. Using 2,584 hours of EEG from 78 participants, we show that nonlinear recurrent forecasting surpasses strong history-aware linear baselines at scale. EEG-World achieves a forecasting correlation of 0.261 versus 0.233 for the strongest history-and-video linear model, with a 3.3-second forecasting-horizon advantage. Its learned dynamics transfer to unseen participants, outperforming the linear baseline in 23 of 24 individuals after calibration. While ongoing EEG history accounts for most predictive performance, controlled stimulus analyses reveal an additional video-dependent component. This component also enables evaluation of visual representations, with V-JEPA 2 improving clip-locked prediction by 35% over combined CLIP and DINOv2 features. Our results demonstrate the value of transferable neural dynamics for individual EEG forecasting and highlight the importance of separating state-driven from stimulus-driven predictability.
item.dc:creator: Junxiang Zhang, Jiayu Zuo, Wenhao Ye, Junfeng Xia, Xiang Chen, Mo Wang, Quanying Liu

item.title: Biomechanically Grounded Prediction of Selective Motor Control and Clinical Outcomes from Infant Video
item.description: arXiv:2611.32890v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Early identification of cerebral palsy (CP) relies on observational assessments of spontaneous infant movement, such as the General Movement Assessment (GMA) and the Baby Observational Selective Control AppRaisal (BabyOSCAR), which require trained raters and substantial scoring time. Existing automated approaches derive hand-engineered features from two-dimensional keypoints, which describe image-plane motion rather than the three-dimensional behavior of individual joints. We present Baby Biomechanical 3D Body (BB3D), an infant-adapted, biomechanical pipeline that estimates joint-angle trajectories from single-camera video. Against a multi-view markerless motion capture reference in 17 infants, BB3D's median Procrustes-aligned error was 17.5~mm for joint centers and 20.4~mm for marker sites. A spatio-temporal transformer, pretrained on BB3D joint-angle trajectories from 1k+ single-camera recordings, and fine-tuned on 550 videos from 350 infants, predicted each individual BabyOSCAR item with a mean within-site AUC of 0.79 and the BabyOSCAR total with a Spearman correlation of 0.86 on held-out recordings. Without being trained on diagnosis, the predicted total separated infants with CP from those without CP with an AUC of 0.86, exceeding a replicated two-dimensional feature classifier (0.67) but below the expert clinician rater's total (0.97). Predicted scores also carried information about functional ability and body distribution, though less than expert clinician scores. These results show that biomechanically grounded representations of monocular video can support scalable, joint-level assessment of selective motor control in infancy
item.dc:creator: Divya Joshi, Ruize Yang, Colleen Peyton, R. James Cotton

item.title: Decision-Native Multimodal Clinical Modeling via Anatomical Grounding and Confidence Calibration
item.description: arXiv:2611.32993v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Structured clinical decisions from volumetric computed tomography (CT) require anatomically grounded predictions and calibrated confidence estimates. However, existing 3D medical multimodal models often suffer from uncalibrated autoregressive decoding and shortcut reliance on irrelevant anatomical regions. We introduce Radev, a decision-native multimodal model that integrates anatomy-guided visual compression, direct candidate prediction, and counterfactual confidence supervision. To bridge global context with fine-grained slice details, a frozen 3D encoder extracts reusable organ-level features, which are dynamically selected by the query to attend to 2D slice features within predicted anatomical bounds. The resulting compact visual tokens enable the language backbone to estimate candidate probabilities in a single forward pass without autoregressive decoding. We further propose Counterfactual-Calibrated Training (CCT) to compare predictions under intact and intervened organ representations. CCT encourages confidence to decrease when removing target-organ evidence degrades decision quality, while penalizing excessive confidence drops under unrelated-organ removal. To facilitate rigorous evaluation, we construct CT-Verdict, a comprehensive benchmark spanning binary finding presence, multiple-choice questions, and ordinal severity assessment across both in-distribution and external cohorts. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Radev significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both decision accuracy and confidence calibration, while generalizing robustly under distribution shifts. Project page at https://juntaojianggavin.github.io/projects/Radev/ .
item.dc:creator: Juntao Jiang, Wenqi Zhong, Guangyu Guo, Dexia Chen, Yilong Hu, Yunhao Bai, Zhenyu Yi, Jianwei Xu, Tony C. W. Mok, Muxuan Gao, Ling Zhang, Yong Liu, Jiangning Zhang, Zhongwei Qiu

item.title: RFW-W: Scaling Physical Asset Universes for Generative Embodied Simulation
item.description: arXiv:2611.33013v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Scaling embodied simulation requires diverse objects with executable physical representations. We present RFW-W, a physical asset universe connecting rigid, articulated, and deformable asset sources to task-conditioned scene composition. Its reported inventories comprise 1,010,386 asset records: 524,611 rigid assets in 1,212 categories (RFW-R), 402,410 articulated assets in 531 categories (RFW-A), and 83,365 jointly verified deformables in 485 categories (RFW-S). These taxonomies contribute 2,228 dataset--category entries. RFW-R couples category-guided generation with collision geometry, composed physical properties, and interaction annotations; RFW-A uses reusable agent-authored procedural generators with explicit part and joint structure; RFW-S uses structure-aware simulation representations, calibration, and independent testing. A common interface preserves physical requirements specific to each asset type for retrieval and scene assembly. Quantitative evaluations demonstrate that RFW-R provides broader asset coverage and stronger scene-fulfillment capabilities than existing datasets. Across five RoboTwin tasks, using 100 demonstrations per task for each asset source, policies trained on RFW-R achieve macro success rates of 71.2% in clean settings and 41.8% under randomization, exceeding the strongest baseline by 15.8 and 10.6 percentage points, respectively. RFW-W provides a scalable and unified asset foundation for generating physically grounded, task-conditioned embodied worlds.
item.dc:creator: Jiawei Weng, Rui Zhang, Saining Zhang, Changjian Pan, Yuanbo Lyu, Jiarui Guo, Yongzhi Li, Guolin Liu, Jialu Liu, Jiankun Wang, Yi Yang, Peishuo Li, Zhiheng Li, Jiaying Wan, Junhao Chen, Weiqing Xiao, Jingrun Du, Wenyi Li, Weiyi Lin, Zenan Meng, Hu Wei, Lin Qu, Zongzheng Zhang, Hao Zhao, Chaojian Li

item.title: Forget Vectors at Play: Universal Input Perturbations Driving Machine Unlearning in Image Classification and Generation
item.description: arXiv:2412.16780v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Machine unlearning (MU), which seeks to erase the influence of specific unwanted data from already-trained models, is becoming increasingly vital in model editing, particularly to comply with evolving data regulations like the "right to be forgotten". Conventional MU approaches are predominantly model-based, typically requiring retraining or fine-tuning the model's weights to meet unlearning requirements. In this work, we approach the MU problem from an input perturbation-based perspective, where the model weights remain intact throughout the unlearning process. We demonstrate the existence of a proactive input-based unlearning strategy, referred to forget vector, which can be generated as an input-agnostic data perturbation and remains as effective as model-based approximate unlearning approaches in both image classification and image generation. For image classification, we demonstrate that forget vector can induce effective class-wise and random data forgetting in frozen classifiers while preserving performance on retained data. We also explore forget vector arithmetic, whereby multiple class-specific forget vectors can be combined through simple operations (e.g., linear combinations) to generate new forget vectors for unseen unlearning tasks, such as forgetting arbitrary subsets across classes. For image generation, we extend forget vector to conditional diffusion models by jointly perturbing the noisy input and conditioning embeddings of frozen denoisers, enabling targeted removal of unwanted classes and concepts from generated outputs. Extensive experiments on both image classification and image generation validate the effectiveness and adaptability of the forget vector, showcasing its competitive performance relative to state-of-the-art model-based methods while achieving superior parameter efficiency.
item.dc:creator: Changchang Sun, Ren Wang, Yihua Zhang, Jinghan Jia, Jiancheng Liu, Gaowen Liu, Yan Yan, Sijia Liu

item.title: SACA: Selective Attention-Based Clustering Algorithm
item.description: arXiv:2508.17150v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Clustering algorithms are fundamental tools across many fields, with density-based methods offering particular advantages in identifying arbitrarily shaped clusters and handling noise. However, their effectiveness is often limited by the requirement of critical parameter tuning by users, which typically requires significant domain expertise. This paper introduces a novel density-based clustering algorithm loosely inspired by the concept of selective attention, designed to minimize reliance on parameter tuning for most applications. The proposed method computes an adaptive threshold to exclude sparsely distributed points and outliers, constructs an initial cluster framework, and subsequently reintegrates the filtered points to refine the final results. Extensive experiments on diverse benchmark datasets demonstrate the robustness, accuracy, and ease of use of the proposed approach, establishing it as a powerful alternative to conventional density-based clustering techniques.
item.dc:creator: Meysam Shirdel Bilehsavar, Razieh Ghaedi, Christian O'Reilly

item.title: In- and Out-of-Distribution Generalization of Reasoning in Multimodal LLMs for Simple Visual Planning Tasks
item.description: arXiv:2602.15460v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Integrating reasoning in (multimodal) large language models has recently led to significant improvement of their capabilities. However, generalization in reasoning models is still vaguely defined and poorly understood. In this work, we present an evaluation framework to rigorously examine how well chain-of-thought (CoT) approaches generalize in simple visual planning, specifically on a grid-based navigation task. The versatility of the task and its data allows us to fine-tune model variants using different input representations (visual and textual) and CoT reasoning strategies, and systematically evaluate them under both in-distribution (ID) and out-of-distribution (OOD) test conditions. Our experiments show that the out-of-distribution generalization (e.g., to larger maps) is largely impacted by the format used for input maps and CoT chains. Surprisingly, we find that coordinate-based reasoning traces which combine text descriptions yield the best OOD generalization. Moreover, CoT reproducing the steps of the A* algorithm yields the state-of-the-art ID accuracy, and simple augmentation of the map solutions seen during training greatly boosts OOD results. Repeating the experiments with maps represented by coordinates yields similar results for another model family. Tests on structurally complex maps reveal a sharp performance drop when shortest solutions require many movement directions or turns. Additional fine-tuning on examples of directionally complex maps substantially recovers this performance. Finally, purely text-based models consistently outperform those utilizing image-based inputs, including a recently proposed approach relying on latent space reasoning.
item.dc:creator: Yannic Neuhaus, Chanoknan Tanchotikul, Nicolas Flammarion, Matthias Hein, Francesco Croce

item.title: 3DSS: 3D Surface Splatting for Inverse Rendering
item.description: arXiv:2605.05876v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present 3D Surface Splatting (3DSS), the first differentiable surface splatting renderer for physically-based inverse rendering from multi-view images. Our central insight is that surface separation, which groups the surfels covering a pixel by the surface they sample, can be formulated with the reconstruction kernels themselves: two surfels sample the same surface when their kernels overlap in depth. Compositing each resulting surface layer with a coverage opacity derived from its accumulated Elliptical Weighted Average (EWA) weight yields anti-aliased silhouettes and informative visibility gradients at sparsely covered edges. With forward microfacet shading under co-optimized HDR environment lighting, 3DSS jointly recovers shape, spatially-varying BRDF, and illumination, and its oriented surfels convert directly into meshes by oriented-point surface reconstruction. On the real-world Stanford-ORB and the TensoIR Synthetic benchmarks, 3DSS outperforms state-of-the-art mesh-based and major comparable implicit and Gaussian-based methods in novel view synthesis and relighting, with geometry on par with the strongest baselines.
item.dc:creator: Mae Younes, Adnane Boukhayma

item.title: A History-Aware Visually Grounded Critic for Computer Use Agents
item.description: arXiv:2606.11078v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Various test-time interventions for Computer Use Agents (CUAs), including critic models, have been developed to improve performance through pre-execution action evaluation in complex Graphical User Interface (GUI) environments. However, existing critics suffer from two key limitations: they (1) focus primarily on short-sighted decision loops (e.g., forgetting earlier actions) and (2) lack the visual grounding needed to detect flawed actions (e.g., clicking wrong UI elements). To address these, we introduce HiViG, a History-aware Visually Grounded test-time framework, built around a multimodal critic trained on real GUI trajectories to abstract past interactions into a compact record and to evaluate actions with visual grounding. At test time, HiViG integrates the critic into the policy decision loop to provide macro-action history, which summarizes the policy's completed achievements, and visually grounded critique, which verifies raw execution coordinates against the current screenshot to intercept errors before execution. Across web, mobile, and desktop benchmarks, HiViG consistently outperforms existing scalar and verbal critics, improving average success rates over the strongest baseline by 5.8% for Qwen3-VL-32B and 9.0% for Gemini-3-Flash, and demonstrates strong cross-platform generalization. Ablations show that macro-action history mitigates short-sighted planning and visually grounded critique reduces execution errors, with both components being critical for test-time scaling in long-horizon GUI tasks.
item.dc:creator: Jaewoo Lee, Zaid Khan, Archiki Prasad, Justin Chih-Yao Chen, Supriyo Chakraborty, Kartik Balasubramaniam, Sambit Sahu, Elias Stengel-Eskin, Hyunji Lee, Mohit Bansal

item.title: Distortion-Corrected Diffusion MRI Using Rotated-View EPI and Joint Field-Map/Image Estimation with Gaussian Primitives
item.description: arXiv:2606.31521v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Echo planar imaging (EPI) is the standard acquisition technique for diffusion and functional neuroimaging, enabling rapid imaging but suffering from geometric distortions caused by B0 field inhomogeneities. Existing correction methods first reconstruct distorted images using parallel imaging, then estimate the B0 field and correct the distortion in the image domain. In this sequential process, reconstruction artifacts at high acceleration factors and low SNR at high diffusion b-values degrade B0 estimation and limit the overall correction quality. We propose a physics-informed framework that jointly estimates the B0 field, the distortion-free image, and the shot-to-shot phase directly from k-space data, without depending on an intermediate parallel-imaging reconstruction. All three are represented as superpositions of Gaussian primitives embedded within an EPI forward model; the explicit, continuous parameterization captures both smooth regions and tissue boundaries and is evaluated on rotated sampling grids without resampling. The diffusion-weighted image is modeled as real and non-negative, with the image phase absorbed into a per-shot phase factor. Acquiring the blip-up/blip-down data at several phase-encoding orientations, the rotated-view principle of PROPELLER applied to full-FOV single-shot EPI, distributes distortions across orientations, improving point spread function isotropy and providing stronger constraints for B0 estimation. On in vivo brain diffusion EPI at R=4 and 5, the proposed method attains the closest brain-boundary agreement with a distortion-free structural reference, with the largest improvement over sequential methods at high b-value.
item.dc:creator: Wenqi Huang, Zhitao Li, Nan Wang, Yimeng Lin, Mengze Gao, Yurui Qian, Sevgi Gokce Kafali, Xiaozhi Cao, Kawin Setsompop, Daniel Rueckert, Congyu Liao

item.title: Instant NuRec: Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Reconstruction for Driving Scene Simulation
item.description: arXiv:2607.14203v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: 3D simulation platforms are critical for autonomous driving because they enable end-to-end policy evaluation, thereby reducing development costs and improving safety. In recent years, neural simulation has become predominant, with methods such as NuRec playing a central role; however, these methods remain relatively slow and typically require per-scene tuning. In this work, we present Instant NuRec, a feed-forward neural reconstruction model that turns a short multi-view driving log into a fully simulatable 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) world in a single forward pass. The model accepts multi-view input from a calibrated camera rig and emits a layered output consisting of static and dynamic 3DGS layers, a sky cubemap, and per-camera ISP corrections, while providing native support for non-pinhole camera models via 3DGUT. It reconstructs a 10-20-second multi-camera scene in roughly 1.5 seconds and achieves a PSNR on the Waymo Open Dataset that is 2.01 dB above the strongest evaluated baseline. Instant NuRec is deeply integrated into NuRec and is compatible with AlpaSim for closed-loop simulation.
item.dc:creator: NVIDIA, :, Jiahui Huang, Jiawei Ren, Michal Tyszkiewicz, Bjoern Haefner, Michael Shelley, Xin Kang, Seung Wook Kim, Ning Xu, Qi Wu, Janick Martinez Esturo, Shengyu Huang, Nick Schneider, Laura Leal-Taixe, Zan Gojcic, Sanja Fidler

item.title: AVENUE: Audio-Video EditiNg Understanding and Evaluation
item.description: arXiv:2609.04253v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Audio-video (AV) editing aims to modify audio and video content according to a target prompt. Unlike single-modality editing, AV editing requires models to infer a modality-selective edit scope from the prompt alone: determining not only what should change, but also which modality should be preserved. Faithfully evaluating such models therefore requires both (i) benchmarks that span diverse edit types and modality categories, and (ii) evaluation that is itself modality-aware and sample-specific. However, existing AV editing benchmarks provide limited coverage of edit types and modality combinations, while current evaluation systems are often modality-blind and sample-agnostic, making it difficult to assess whether models faithfully preserve the unintended modality. To address these gaps, we introduce AVENUE, Audio-Video EditiNg Understanding and Evaluation, comprising two contributions: (1) a benchmark of 1,291 source clips and 7,957 editing instructions across audio-targeted, video-targeted, and AV-coupled edit types, curated and human-verified from VGGSound; and (2) a sample-specific, modality-aware evaluation framework that specifies, for each sample, both the intended change and the content that must remain intact. We evaluate representative AV editing models spanning three editing paradigms : joint, sequential, and separate, providing the first systematic analysis of modality-selectivity across paradigms. Our findings reveal a fundamental open challenge: when editing one modality, existing models frequently induce unintended changes in the other, regardless of paradigm. AVENUE provides a benchmark and modality-aware evaluation framework to drive progress toward more controllable AV editing models. Our dataset is publicly available on Hugging Face: https://huggingface.co/datasets/AVENUE-dataset/AVENUE.
item.dc:creator: Hayeon Kim, Yoojin Jang, Jaejun Yoo

item.title: Self-Distilling Future Video Representations for World Action Models
item.description: arXiv:2610.30320v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: World Action Models (WAMs) have emerged as a promising approach to learning generalist robot policies using rich spatiotemporal priors from pre-trained video diffusion models. A recent line of WAMs improves inference efficiency by conditioning a separate action decoder on intermediate future video representations extracted from a single denoising step, avoiding costly iterative denoising required for video generation. This design makes action prediction depend directly on the quality of these future representations. In this paper, we introduce Future REpresentation learning via self-Distillation with temporal context (FRED), a framework that trains WAMs to improve the quality of future video representations from noise in a single denoising step. Specifically, FRED uses self-distillation to predict future representations from noise, using representations extracted from ground-truth future observations as targets. We further condition the video model on historical observations, providing temporal context for predicting future representations better. Across diverse real-world manipulation scenarios, FRED consistently outperforms competing WAMs. It achieves particularly large gains on long-horizon and out-of-domain tasks under zero-shot environment generalization, and substantially improves human-to-robot skill transfer, reaching 50.0% task success on tasks absent from robot training data and demonstrated only in human videos, compared with 10.7% for the best competing WAM.
item.dc:creator: Huiwon Jang, Suhyeok Jang, Hyeonmo Kang, Seungku Kim, Jinwoo Shin, Sihyun Yu

item.title: Direct Conditioning of Audio Diffusion Transformers on fMRI Reveals Cortical Contributions to Sound Reconstruction
item.description: arXiv:2611.12603v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Reconstructing audio from brain activity remains challenging. Existing brain-to-audio pipelines typically map neural responses to predefined stimulus representations before synthesis. While recent work in the visual domain has explored direct conditioning on brain activity, this approach has not yet been extended to audio diffusion models. We introduce MAAS (Multi-Area Auditory Synthesis), an end-to-end framework that conditions a pretrained audio diffusion transformer on ROI-wise fMRI responses without first supervising a decoder to predict an external stimulus representation. MAAS uses region-specific projections and learned brain tokens to condition Stable Audio through a dedicated cross-attention pathway. On a 7T fMRI dataset, we demonstrate consistent improvements over baselines, including two-stage fMRI-to-latent conditioning, across both acoustic and semantic evaluation metrics. In addition, we introduce a fidelity metric grounded in a computational model of auditory neural processing, which allows us to quantify the contribution of individual auditory cortical regions to reconstructed audio representations.
item.dc:creator: Matteo Ciferri, Tonio Weidler, Matteo Ferrante, Nicola Toschi, Elia Formisano

item.title: Envisioning Agentic Robotics: A New Era of Robotic Systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.18359v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The release of GPT-6 Astra marks the emergence of a new paradigm in robotics: agentic robotics. Within weeks, frontier models with agentic harnesses matched or exceeded task-specific policies on many embodied benchmarks. Instead of training a dedicated policy for each family of tasks, an agentic robotic system applies a foundation model to open-world embodied tasks. It operates in a closed loop: observing the environment, interpreting user intent, reasoning about the task, invoking skills and tools, verifying outcomes, and adapting its strategy. Despite these advances, the community has yet to converge on a shared definition, a reliable evaluation framework, or a research roadmap. We argue that Embodied System 2, realized by a foundation model together with an embodied harness, forms the decision-making core of agentic robotics. Its central challenge is to translate general-purpose reasoning into effective and verifiable actions under physical constraints such as limited reaction time, mechanical limits, unpredictable environment changes, and irreversible consequences. Motivated by this perspective, we propose an evaluation framework that measures both model capabilities and closed-loop system performance. Furthermore, we identify the principles that carry over from digital to physical agents and the challenges that must be addressed to achieve reliable physical autonomy. On top of the Embodied System 2 and the evaluation framework, we envision a research roadmap toward sustained autonomy: the ability to perform work safely and reliably with progressively broader responsibility, from executing individual primitives to fulfilling standing roles.
item.dc:creator: Grid Robotics, :, Qingfeng Lan, Duo Li, Siyao Li, Yiheng Lyu, Shijian Lu, Zhenghao Qi, Shizun Wang, Xinchao Wang, Ming Yang, Zhiqin Yang, Zuhao Yang, Tao Yu

item.title: TacInno: Teaching Vision-Language-Action Models the Contact Dynamics Beyond Vision and Action
item.description: arXiv:2611.26405v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have recently been equipped with tactile sensing to perceive visually subtle contact events in contact-rich manipulation. However, adding tactile input yields inconsistent gains, and some visuo-tactile VLA models rely little on tactile input, because much of the tactile change, such as the gel deformation during gripper closure, is predictable from visual observations and executed actions. To address this problem, we introduce TacInno, which isolates the contact dynamics that vision and executed actions cannot explain, termed tactile innovation, and uses tactile innovation only as a training target. Specifically, the TacInno tokenizer, conditioned on visual observations and executed actions, compresses the future tactile change into a discrete code, and the policy, TacInno-VLA, learns to predict the code, adding no module for the code at deployment. TacInno-VLA achieves average success rates of 87.5% across six simulation tasks and 70.5% across four real-world tasks, outperforming the strongest visuo-tactile baseline by 10.7 and 9.0 percentage points, respectively. Ablation studies validate the contributions of visual and action conditioning, multi-frame encoding, and auxiliary code prediction. Together, these results demonstrate the effectiveness of tactile innovation as a supervision signal for contact-rich manipulation.
item.dc:creator: Weile Li, Yunfan Lou, Muqing Shi, Zihao Zhang, Zhenbiao Huang, Boxian Yao, Xiyu Zhu, Zhibo Pang

item.title: Beyond Code and Pixels: Co-Generating Editable and Visually Rich Presentations
item.description: arXiv:2611.28010v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Generating PPTX presentations is a structured task that requires semantic planning, visual composition, precise layout, and editability, motivating collaboration among specialized agents. However, programmatic methods offer editability but often produce rigid designs, while image-based methods provide visual richness but flatten content into difficult-to-edit pixels. A hybrid system can combine these strengths, but must coordinate interdependent decisions across content, layout, and appearance. To address this challenge, we propose SlidesWeaver, a hybrid multi-agent system that coordinates language and vision agents through shared deck- and slide-level states. Specifically, it uses staged multimodal commitment, diffusion-based composition planning, and two generation schedules for different priorities between composition freedom and accurate text preservation, while preserving native text and geometry. Across 1,728 generations spanning 24 system-model configurations, SlidesWeaver achieves consistently superior overall quality across all evaluated dimensions while maintaining structural control, editability, and practical generation efficiency.
item.dc:creator: Wenrui Zhou, Jiashun Liu, Sujie Hu, Bang Liu, Ling Pan

item.title: CONCOR: Benchmarking Contrastive Decoding for Visual Hallucination Mitigation Beyond Final-Output Performance
item.description: arXiv:2611.30460v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Contrastive decoding (CD) mitigates object hallucination in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) by contrasting token distributions under different conditions to adjust token scores. However, existing generative and discriminative benchmarks primarily measure final task scores, which can be confounded by candidate filtering, changes in generation trajectories, and response biases, making it difficult to isolate the effects of the underlying contrastive adjustments. To address these limitations while complementing existing evaluations, we introduce CONCOR (Contrastive Correction Evaluation), a controlled benchmark that directly evaluates the competition between ground-truth and different types of hallucinated candidates using the Contrastive Grounding Margin (CGM). CGM also enables analysis of directional consistency, composition, and reliability of contrastive corrections. Our evaluation reveals that existing CD methods exhibit distinct correction behaviors: some consistently favor ground-truth candidates, whereas others produce strong corrections but also introduce more errors. Crucially, these differences help explain their contrasting responses to increased contrast strength, which improves some methods while degrading others. These findings highlight the importance of evaluating the contrastive correction itself, rather than relying solely on final-output performance, and CONCOR provides a controlled and interpretable framework for understanding and improving CD methods for hallucination mitigation.
item.dc:creator: Ting Chen, Geng Li, Guohao Chen, Hanjia Lyu

item.title: MOZAIC: An Audio-Video Deepfake Benchmark for Telling What Is Fake
item.description: arXiv:2611.31301v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Audio-video (AV) deepfakes can fake the face, the voice, or both. Most benchmarks only ask whether a clip is real or fake, so they cannot show whether a detector relies on the picture, the voice, or encoding traces. We present MOZAIC, a paired benchmark with a 4-way label in which every source clip is released in all four combinations of real or fake video and real or fake audio so each modality contribution can be measured directly. Fakes cover inner-face swapping, whole-frame video diffusion and voice conversion. MOZAIC has 137,745 clips from 15,014 source pairs and four tasks: T1 AV authenticity, T2 manipulation type, T3 identity verification and T4 explanation. We evaluate 12 AV multimodal LLMs (MLLMs), train four detectors and fine-tune MLLMs with LoRA. Overall, the best MLLM reaches only 35.6% on the four-way T1 and catches far more video-only fakes than voice-only fakes (43.6% vs 7.5%). Trained detectors reach 98.4% on T1, and LoRA fine-tuning raises explanation scores (OmniVinci 4.17 to 7.40, Qwen2.5-Omni 4.42 to 6.98), but the best T1 detector falls to 78.3% when the face-swap generator is held out of training, so generalization and explanation remain open. We release the dataset, the compact MOZAIC-SMALL split, the code and the prompts. https://vectorinstitute.github.io/mozaic/
item.dc:creator: Shaina Raza, Mohamed Hafez, Ahmed Y. Radwan, Khalid Elgazzar, Kathryn Hume

item.title: OVOK: A Recursive Self-Improving Agentic Framework for Video-Based Articulated Robot State Estimation
item.description: arXiv:2611.32185v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recovering articulated robot state from video supports metric spatial sensing for manipulation, scene reconstruction, and action planning. Yet the problem is ill-posed: different intrinsics, camera-to-robot poses, and joint angles can explain similar observations. Prior task-specific regressors typically assume known intrinsics, fit one robot through laborious data collection and robot-specific training, and still transfer poorly across scenes. Foundation models apply to any robot zero-shot, but their estimates have large errors. We present OVOK (One Video to Kinetics), a recursive self-improving agentic framework for this task. Under a human-authored protocol, an agentic initializer constructs robot-specific OVOK-4k; a proposer--executor--verifier loop then jointly evolves tools and executable workflows from feedback. Updated tools and workflows are accepted only when the verifier judges a positive improvement. The retained workflow is frozen for accurate inference. Experiments demonstrate that the evolved workflow achieves state-of-the-art results on DREAM-V and RoboKeyGen-V, delivering robust and accurate estimates.
item.dc:creator: Cheng Dai, Renkai Luo, Guanfeng Tang, Siming Li, Hao Zhao

item.title: OmniAct: One Policy, One Million Embodiments
item.description: arXiv:2611.33158v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A single policy that controls diverse robots must not only transfer task knowledge across embodiments, but also adapt its behavior to each robot's capabilities. Existing approaches facilitate transfer through shared action representations, but these representations do not necessarily capture how differences in robot morphology should shape manipulation strategies. We introduce OmniAct, a cross-embodiment manipulation policy that conditions directly on each robot's kinematics in a specific scene to produce embodiment-specific behavior. This kinematic graph represents the robot's joint positions, motion axes, and connectivity to its visual observation, allowing the policy to account for how its embodiment related to objects and surfaces in the scene. A flow-matching policy predicts relative joint motions for each node, enabling control across robots with different degrees of freedom and kinematic configurations. To learn how physical structure shapes behavior at scale, we procedurally design and filter one million physically feasible robot embodiments; next, we develop algorithms to generate robot trajectories in simulation for all embodiments; finally, we train across diverse simulated manipulation tasks. On 2,000 embodiment-scene-held-out evaluation episodes, OmniAct achieves 63.0% success, compared to 17.8% for pi 0.5 and 57.9% for the strongest baseline; on the task families GPT-6 Astra was evaluated on, it achieves 64.7% against GPT-6 Astra's 41.1%. On a previously unseen real-world robot, it achieves nearly twice the success rate of the next best method, MolmoAct2. Beyond task success, we observe that OmniAct learns distinct manipulation strategies that exploit the capabilities and accommodate the limitations of different morphologies. Project: https://omniact.github.io/
item.dc:creator: Xiang Fan, Yuheng Wang, Jiayuan Yan, Bohan Fang, Wisdom Oluchi Ikezogwo, Ainaz Eftekhar, Max Argus, Zhongzheng Ren, Jiafei Duan, Ranjay Krishna
